Subject: ACME - Post-call TCO recap & next steps

Hi Alice / Bob —

Thanks again for your time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we’re aligned and so I can pull together a one-page TCO that meets your budget constraints.

Call highlights / pain we heard:
- Heavy per-call Q&A workload from support KBs (~30M tokens/month estimated from current traffic).
- Peak latency sensitivity for live agent assist (p95 target <= 250ms).
- Procurement/finance looking at run-rate budget of ~$30k/month for inference.

Goals you shared:
1) Reduce average handle time on agent workflows by 20-30% while keeping latency SLOs.
2) Stay within the finance target of ~ $30k/month; prefer predictable monthly spend.
3) Keep customer data in a dedicated environment (VPC/Dedicated) for compliance.

Redwood levers we discussed (cost & performance):
- Model selection: switch from a 13B dense model to a quantized 7B variant for lower cost if quality acceptable.
- Batching + continuous KV caching: reduce token compute by ~15-25% for repeat prefixes.
- Prefix caching for common prompts (support templates) to avoid repeated token generation.
- Reserved (Dedicated) capacity: offers a lower per-token rate and predictable billing vs burst/hosted.
- Prompt engineering + compression: shorter prompts and instruction templates to reduce tokens.

Initial back-of-envelope token economics (rough, for alignment):
- Current: ~30M input+output tokens/month x $0.00006/token = $1,800/month raw compute (hosted rates vary) — (note: example numbers for discussion)
- With higher service levels/latency and Hosted API model: expected $20k-$45k/month depending on model and throughput.
- Dedicated reserved capacity + 7B quantized + caching/batching: target ~$20k-$28k/month (within your $30k constraint) depending on commit level and cache hit rates.

Attachments I’m including:
- Acme-MAP.xlsx (mutual action plan)
- redwood-pricing-sheet.pdf (sample pricing bands and reserved capacity examples)

Requested next steps / asks:
1) Can you confirm the monthly token estimate range we discussed (30M +/- 30%) so I can run two scenarios?
2) What’s the procurement timeline for a committed monthly spend? (PO lead time / approval window)
3) If you’re open, I’ll schedule a 30-min follow-up next week to walk the 1-page TCO and recommend A/B plan (conservative vs aggressive).

If you confirm the token range and procurement timeline I’ll finalize the one-pager and put together a recommended committed capacity that fits the $30k ceiling.

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise SDR, Redwood Inference

Redwood Inference

Procurement timeline: likely 3-4 weeks once we land on pricing and SOW; procurement needs an approved SOW/quote and security questionnaire completed.

Yes to a follow-up next week. Can you do Tue 30th at 10am PT? We’d like a short TCO page to present to finance ahead of the call.

FYI — forwarded Alice’s confirmation. Budget is firm at ~$30k/mo and procurement is ~3-4w. They confirmed ~30M tokens/month.

Proposed approach (recommendation for the quoting pack):
- Option A (recommended): Dedicated Reserved pool sized for 40M tokens/month with KV/prefix caching + 7B quantized model. Estimated committed cost ~ $24k/month. Includes 99.9% uptime SLA and VPC deployment.
- Option B (lower commit): Hosted dedicated with autoscale to handle bursts, conservative per-token pricing, estimated ~$32k/mo but no long-term commit required.

Key asks for the pricing pack:
1) Vivek — can infra confirm p95 latency for 7B quantized on our Dedicated profiles under agent-assist workload (seq len 256, concurrency 40)? We need numbers to justify tradeoffs to ACME’s SREs.
2) Neha — can you draft a 1-page TCO that compares A vs B with simple ROI math: current cost of agent time (avg handle time reduction) vs incremental infra? I’ll attach the MAP and pricing sheet.

I’ll prepare a short slide + the one-pager and send to Alice ahead of Tue 30th call. If you have a quick model for cache hit assumptions (10/20/30%) that’d help.

Thanks — Marissa
